title: rolling-observability-upgrades-tenant-alert-suppression-and-rollback-playbook
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces tenant-aware alert suppression window during observability upgrades; adds a rolling upgrade controller for Prometheus/Grafana Helm releases; Terraform flag for controlled dashboard provisioning; rollback playbook and test harness for on-prem private installs.
description:
Motivation: Upgrading the observability stack in private installs (Prometheus + Grafana + log-shippers) has been causing alert storms and noisy pager traffic when dashboards and recording rules change out-of-band. This PR implements a safe, rolling upgrade path that suppresses tenant-scoped alerts during the critical window, provisions dashboards atomically, and provides an automated rollback playbook for fast recovery.

What I changed (high level): Added a small Kubernetes controller (helm-hooked) that sequences Grafana dashboard provisioning and PrometheusRule application with tenant-scoped suppression annotations; added a Terraform variable alert_silence_window (seconds) to the observability module; updated Helm charts to include pre-upgrade hooks that create Silence objects and a post-upgrade verifier; introduced an immutable-folder import mode for Grafana provisioning to avoid transient duplicate dashboards; added e2e test harness which exercises upgrades across 3 tenant namespaces and validates no firing alerts during silence window.

Commits: 1) controller: implement rolling upgrade sequencer and tenant label propagation; 2) helm: pre/post hooks + grafana immutable-folder mode; 3) terraform: expose alert_silence_window and canary_namespace for staged upgrades; 4) tests: integration harness and playbook docs; 5) docs: upgrade/rollback runbook.

Files changed (selected): charts/grafana/templates/pre-upgrade-hook.yaml (new), charts/grafana/templates/post-upgrade-check.yaml (modified), modules/observability/main.tf (var+outputs), modules/observability/README.md (docs), pkg/controllers/upgrade/sequencer.go (new, ~420 LOC), test/e2e/upgrade_safety_test.go (new), docs/upgrade_playbook.md (new).

Testing: Local kind cluster + Prometheus/Grafana chart pinned to test fixtures. Ran CI integration suite (observability-e2e) which reproduces tenant alerting workload; CI passed after fixing race in sequencer reconciler (addressed by commit 3). Manual dry-run performed on internal staging private-installer with two tenants; observed no alert firing during the configured silence window and dashboards landed in immutable folders as expected.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag 'obs_rolling_upgrades' in installer config; 2) Enable in canary region with alert_silence_window=180s and canary_namespace set; 3) Monitor token-level and per-tenant alert counts on Redwood Console dashboards for 24 hours; 4) Gradually increase rollout to all private installs.

Rollback playbook (high level): - If post-upgrade verifications fail, controller triggers a Helm rollback of the Grafana release and removes Silence objects; - Run 'installer rollback-playbook --snapshot <pre-upgrade-snapshot>' to restore PrometheusRule and dashboard state; - Run validation harness from test/e2e to confirm alerts have returned to baseline. Detailed steps live in docs/upgrade_playbook.md.

Review thread (summary): - Liam: requested explicit tenant label propagation and unit tests for sequencer; added two unit tests and clarified label handling in sequencer.go. - Sofia: asked for an audit log entry when silences are created; added controller emit of Kubernetes Events and a short note in README. - Ethan: asked for terraform variable naming clarity; renamed alert_window_seconds -> alert_silence_window and updated module README. All reviewers approved.

CI status: GitHub Actions matrix ran unit, lint, helm template, terraform validate, and observability-e2e. Observability-e2e initially failed due to race; fixed in commit 3 and all checks passed on re-run.

Backward compatibility: No breaking API changes for customers. Optional feature flag controls behavior. The terraform variable defaults to 0 (no silence) to preserve existing installs unless explicitly configured.

Notes and follow-ups: - Proposed follow-up: autoscale silence window based on number of tenants and rule churn (ENG-2027) - Consider adding a dry-run mode to sequencer for dry verification before committing to production.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI.
